findings.observation: Used vision tool to examine Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan). The key notes identify one proposed bike rack (key note #1), which is located near the building entrance on private property, not in the ROW. Vision analysis confirmed no bike racks, benches, trash receptacles, awnings, or canopies are shown within the public right-of-way. The only streetscape elements in ROW are standard infrastructure: sidewalks, street trees (addressed separately under CC-24-04), existing traffic signs, and proposed fire hydrants.
findings.reasoning: This item applies only IF streetscape elements (awnings, canopies, benches, bike racks, trash receptacles) are proposed in ROW. Vision analysis specifically confirmed that the one bike rack shown on plans is on private property. No other covered streetscape elements are proposed in ROW. Standard elements like sidewalks and fire hydrants are not 'streetscape elements' under this License Agreement category.
findings.explanation: No streetscape elements (awnings, canopies, benches, bike racks, trash) in ROW; bike rack is on private property.

findings.observation: Used vision tool to examine Sheet 51 (Planting Plan). Vision analysis confirmed that proposed street trees ARE shown along all street frontages including along the curved frontages and straight street frontages. The trees are located in typical planting zones between the street curb and property line, which constitutes public ROW. Sheet 14 also shows a '5' PLANTING ZONE' along Collier Street within the ROW. However, the Consolidated Site Plan Application (Section 6, Property Attributes, page 3-4) shows the answer to 'Will a License Agreement Application be submitted for this project?' is checked NO.
findings.reasoning: Street trees and landscaping are clearly proposed within the public ROW along multiple street frontages (Collier St, S Lamar Blvd, and other frontages). Per Austin's requirements, any street trees, landscaping, or irrigation in ROW requires a License Agreement. The application explicitly states NO License Agreement will be submitted. This creates a direct conflict: the plans show improvements requiring a License Agreement, but the application states none will be submitted.
findings.explanation: Street trees and landscaping proposed in ROW (shown on Sheet 51 and Sheet 14), but application indicates no License Agreement will be submitted.

(>300 LF OF W/WW PIPING IN ROW)' and the YES box is checked. The form states 'IF YES, PLEASE PROVIDE UCC#' and shows '(pending)'. This indicates the applicant has acknowledged the AULCC requirement and the case number is pending. The project is NOT in DAPCZ per facts.md, so the 300 LF threshold (not 25 LF) applies. The AW Infrastructure table on Sheet 6 shows water and wastewater infrastructure proposed.
findings.reasoning: The applicant has properly indicated on Sheet 6 that AULCC review is required because excavations exceed 300 LF outside DAPCZ. The case number is shown as pending, which is acceptable at completeness check stage as long as the requirement is acknowledged and will be provided. The plans clearly reference the AULCC requirement and indicate coordination is underway.
findings.explanation: AULCC requirement acknowledged on Sheet 6 with pending case number for >300 LF of water/wastewater piping in ROW.

Since no License Agreement has actually been submitted (per the application) and no tower crane is proposed, the condition 'when License Agreement or tower crane is involved' is not met. The fact that a License Agreement SHOULD be submitted (per CC-24-04) is a separate deficiency. This item checks whether AULCC was coordinated IF those triggers exist, but they don't currently exist in the submittal.
